meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Was Owen asked about it before you entered it?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58; I'm writing those down. He wrote it over the weekend, so pasting it into a new file is not a crime. Turn the screen.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. A paste shows where the words landed, Hale, not who wrote them.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misquote Shakespeare every day, and a bad citation is a mark off, not a zero. What else?
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Outlines exist so a student can change his mind. Show me both.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

So you did speak to him, the day before. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by a teacher he says has had it in for him since September goes blank. Is that note written down anywhere he could see it?
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the book open, that's not a comparison. And you still haven't said what you want, Hale. What are you proposing?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then leave it out of this room. What are you proposing?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, private, nowhere near his classmates, and marked before December 1. Before I agree to anything, turn that screen and show me the version history and both of those documents.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?

To put this behind him, yes, a private rewrite, marked before December 1, with nothing on his file. I want all of it in an email tonight, with copies of every document you've described attached. He's done nothing wrong, Hale; this just ends it.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, November 12, after school. Put the day and time in tonight's email. Ten minutes.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday after school, marked before December 1, and the documents attached to that email. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Owen hears about Thursday from you, in person, not from his phone.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12 after school, that its mark will replace the zero before December 1, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that in writing, with copies of every document you described attached, and that you tell Owen about Thursday in person. I expect it tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight with the documents attached and Owen told in person; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: you told her you had spoken to Owen on November 2 and written a note that day, because it answered the procedural question she walked in with, whether he was heard before the zero.
What cost ground: you described the version history and the outline but never actually turned the screen, so none of her defences were ever answered and the deal rested on volume rather than on anything she had checked.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said a paste shows where the words landed and not who wrote them, pull up the history right then and ask where the weekend draft is, so that piece stands before you move to the next.
